sources: CRA — What is a business? (canada.ca, page details 2026-08-31) · current · 'A business is an activity that you intend to carry on for profit and there is evidence to support that intention'; CRA looks at each case on its own merits; unreported income can bring a 10% penalty

CRA — Income Tax Audit Manual, ch. 27.2 'Pursuit of profit' (canada.ca) · current · Stewart v. Canada (SCC 2002) two-stage test: pursuit of profit or personal endeavour, then business or property; activities with a personal element must be carried on in a sufficiently commercial manner; objective factors include profit and loss history, training, intended course of action, capability to show a profit; a hobby only where the personal element substantially displaces commerciality; no source → no business income and no business loss
CRA T4127 (Jan 2026) and CPP 2026, via b9/calc.py · 2026 · tax + CPP for a Manitoba employee with a $60,000 salary plus self-employment income

Calculation (not a CRA rule): b1/calc.py → data.json. $60,000 salary; cakes: sales $8,000 − costs $3,000 = $5,000 profit → as a business: +$1,485.58 tax + $595.00 CPP = $2,080.58. First-year loss: $2,000 − $3,500 = −$1,500 → as a business it lowers income: $460.53 back; as a hobby: no income, no loss ($0). Dependencies: the facts of each case (intent, records, pricing, marketing, plan, profit history); other income; province; GST/HST is a separate test. Amounts are an example.

yt.description:
You sell cakes on weekends. Hobby or business? CRA has a test, and it changes your taxes.

CRA: a business is an activity you intend to carry on for profit, with evidence to support that intention. Evidence means facts: prices, records, marketing, a plan, a real chance of profit. If it's a personal pastime, there's no business income, and no business loss either.

Example (Manitoba, 2026): a $60,000 day job, cake sales $8,000, ingredients $3,000 = $5,000 profit.
• As a business: about $2,081 in tax + CPP.
• First year at a loss: $2,000 − $3,500 = −$1,500. As a business, that loss lowers the salary income: about $461 back. As a hobby: $0.

Selling on Etsy? Does Etsy tell CRA? Yes or no, guess below.

Sources: CRA 'What is a business?'; CRA Income Tax Audit Manual ch. 27 (Stewart v. Canada, 2002 SCC); CRA T4127 2026 rates, CPP 2026. Example only; general information, not tax advice.
